leverage.exposure: None open and none created. The balance is positive, no leveraged position is outstanding, and the recommended structure is built so that it never opens one: the buy is bid below the envelope the funding sale will cover, with a deliberate buffer against tonight's market-value tick, and the auction settles with most of a day still to run before the lock. The failure mode to guard against is not the recommended move but a second bid alongside it — two simultaneous wins could not be funded and would carry a negative balance into the lock, which scores zero for the whole matchday. The other failure mode is selling first: if the auction is lost and the sale has already gone through, the squad is at ten and takes the under-eleven penalty.

binding_gap: The gap is capacity, not quality. With exactly eleven players and almost no cash, the squad can only improve by selling into a buy, and the sale has to be worth less in points than the buy adds while being worth more in money than the buy costs. Only one body in the squad satisfies both halves, and that is Conte — which is why the whole run turns on his slot. The deeper version of the same problem, and the one to carry forward, is that the weakest player in the eleven is also the cheapest, so the largest available upgrade is permanently out of reach: fixing the worst slot would need money that only the good slots can raise, and selling a good slot costs more points than the fix gains. That does not resolve until the squad grows past twelve and a real sale exists.

verdict.detail: There is a move this run, and it reverses a call the ledger made this morning. Buy Satoshi Tanaka off the Kickbase board and, only once he has actually landed, instant-sell Bambase Conte to Kickbase. That takes the eleven from 4-3-3 to 4-4-2 and swaps the lowest-scoring outfielder in the fielded eleven for a news-confirmed Schalke starter. The earlier AVOID on Tanaka rested on two legs and both have expired: it judged him against Onyeka, which was the wrong displacement — a midfielder bought into this squad is funded by the Conte sale and lands in a 4-4-2, so the man he replaces is Conte — and it reserved the single unwind slot for the Mokwa structure, which died when Mokwa was lost. Nothing else on the board is both affordable and points-positive. The balance is positive, the squad is legal, every player is fit, and if the auction is lost the correct action is to do nothing at all.

sell.reason: Conte, conditionally, and only as the second leg. He is fit and he is not being dropped on merit of fitness — this run's league-wide injury sweep gives Hoffenheim only one absentee and it is not him. He is a rotation player with one start in three appearances and he is the lowest-scoring outfielder in the fielded eleven, which is the entire case. The instrument is the instant sale to Kickbase, which has paid exactly market value every time this ledger has measured it, and his value is rising, so settling after tonight's tick should pay more rather than less. The guard is absolute and it is the same guard that fired correctly when Mokwa was lost: if the Tanaka auction does not land, this sale must not happen. Selling him with the squad at eleven drops it to ten and triggers the under-eleven penalty, which would cost more than his points are worth. Nothing else in the squad is a sale. Sirch is the weakest body but selling him funds nothing and opens the same hole.

buy.reason: Tanaka is the recommendation and the reasoning is as much about winnability as about merit. His scoring average is the highest of the three affordable midfielders, and because his market value is the lowest of the three the Conte envelope buys a far larger premium over that value than it would on either alternative — which matters, because every contested auction this ledger has lost was lost by bidding a premium computed from older, cheaper clears. The news is dated and clean: Schalke's club page from the seventh puts him in the probable eleven for the Friday match at Union Berlin, his profile reads fit, and there is a dated starting guarantee and a dated manager's endorsement behind it. The honest mark against him, recorded rather than buried, is that his average comes from a single start and his participation rate is low, so expect it to regress; even haircut, the swap still gains. Chuki is the runner-up and he loses on funding, not on merit — a two-match average, confirmed in Werder's probable eleven, but his higher market value leaves a ceiling bid below the clears that comparable bodies have gone for. Stalmach would have been the buy on paper, cheapest of the three with a genuine two-match average, and dated news refuses him: Werder's own probable eleven starts Chuki and leaves him on the bench. Do not bid on more than one of them. Two wins cannot be funded even by selling both Conte and Sirch, and would leave a negative balance at the lock, which scores nothing for the entire matchday. Pavlovic is the best player on the board and Saibari the second-best attacker, and both are refused purely because no single sale comes close to funding them; Da Costa is the painful near miss, the right body in the right structure and short of the envelope by less than half a million before any premium.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. Every manager ask on the board sits above market value, so the mechanism a flip depends on is simply absent, and the board listings all price at market value exactly, which leaves nothing to arbitrage. What is visible instead is a rival cycling cheap bodies through the board and back to Kickbase for fractions of a percent, several times an hour; that is motion rather than points and it is not a model to copy. One genuinely useful reading did come out of the day's transfers: two manager-to-manager sales cleared well above the band this ledger had measured for such deals, so the old benchmark for a manager ask is stale and has been widened. That changes how a future ask should be judged, though it rescues none of the asks currently standing. Separately, a cheap defender cleared at a premium several times anything previously measured on a body of that size, which is a reminder that small-money board auctions in this league run hot.

fitness.sweep: Nothing new and nothing wrong. Every one of the eleven carries a clean status flag, and a league-wide injury and suspension sweep read today clears all seven clubs the squad draws on: the listed absentees at Augsburg, Dortmund, Leipzig, Paderborn, Elversberg and Hoffenheim include none of the squad, and Bayern have none at all. No squad player is newly injured, suspended, benched or the subject of dated news about leaving the league. On the buy side, both shortlisted midfielders were checked against dated club pages rather than against their scoring averages, and that check is what separated them: one is in his club's probable eleven and the other, on the same page, is not.
